name: nucleo-h753zi
comment: A Nucleo-144 board carrying an STM32H753ZI: dual-core Cortex-M7 at 480 MHz with an M4 co-processor, 2 MB of flash, and 1 MB of RAM across several banks. Programmed through the ST-LINK already on the board.

flash.comment: 2 MB, the whole of the on-chip flash

ram.comment: 128 KB of data TCM, where the stack and the data live. DTCM rather than the AXI SRAM: it is core-coupled, it is reachable from the moment the core runs, and it is what the vendor's own linker script for this board uses.

dtcm.comment: 128 KB of data TCM: the fastest RAM, reachable by the core only and not by DMA

sram1.comment: 288 KB of SRAM1 on the D2 domain

sram2.comment: 64 KB of SRAM2 on the D3 domain

bkpsram.comment: 4 KB of backup SRAM, which survives a reset that is not a power cycle

axiram.comment: 512 KB of AXI SRAM, the largest region a DMA transfer can reach. Not where the stack goes: it is behind a domain that has to be configured first.

flash.command: openocd -f interface/stlink.cfg -f target/stm32h7x.cfg -c "program {binary} verify reset exit"
flash.comment: Flashing reaches the part through the ST-LINK, which every Nucleo-144 board carries

CONSOLE_TX.comment: Connected to the ST-LINK virtual COM port

supply.comment: The Nucleo-144 boards take their core supply through the LDO. The CMSIS startup leaves Run* mode according to this, and a part left in Run* mode faults on its first access to flash.

debug.comment: The vendor's register map for this part, from the CMSIS device data repository. A project that carries its own keeps it: what a project has committed to it is a fact about the project, and this is only consulted when nothing does.
